mainTopic: The rules for choosing the פסוקים of מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות; which prayer leader blows שופר and which says הלל; why ראש השנה has no הלל; and why the שופר does not override יום טוב prohibitions.
overview: The גמרא first gives examples of פסוקים that are not said in מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות because they speak of anger against ישראל. Verses about punishing the נכרים are allowed, but a זכרון verse about a יחיד is not, even when it is for good. Next comes a series of disputes between רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה about which פסוקים count. They argue about פקדונות verses, how many times a passage counts as מלכות, and whether a פסוק with only 'תרועה' counts as a שופר verse. The גמרא then works out that רבי יוסי prefers to end each section with a פסוק from the תורה. It answers that he has enough מלכיות verses because he counts 'שמע ישראל' and similar פסוקים. A new משנה gives the שופר to the מוסף leader and הלל to the שחרית leader. רבי יוחנן explains that the שופר was moved later during a time of persecution. רבי אבהו explains that there is no הלל on ראש השנה because it is a day of judgment. A final משנה teaches that the מצוה of שופר does not override יום טוב prohibitions, and the גמרא explains why: one עשה cannot push aside both an עשה and a לא תעשה.

steps.title: An example of a forbidden kingship verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives an example of a מלכיות verse that speaks of punishment: 'with fury poured out, will I be King over you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Kingship verses, for example: 'As I live, says the Lord God, surely with a mighty hand, and with an outstretched arm, and with fury poured out, will I be King over you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה's rule against punishment verses by giving a real example from the מלכיות category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This verse is about God being King, so it clearly belongs to the מלכיות category. But it describes that kingship coming with anger ('fury poured out'). That is why it falls under the משנה's ban on פורענות verses.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
The section of ראש השנה מוסף about God's Kingship

phrases.english: Gemara: Kingship verses, for example:
"As I live, says the Lord God,
surely with a mighty hand
and with an outstretched arm
and with fury poured out, will I be King over you,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה's ruling against פורענות verses by giving an example.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מלכיות verse that describes God's Kingship coming with anger is not said on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Even anger that leads to redemption is not mentioned
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן saw this verse as positive, since anger like this would lead to redemption. Even so, it is left out, because we do not mention anger on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though רב נחמן said, 'Any anger like this, let the Holy One, blessed be He, be angry at us and redeem us,' since the verse was said in anger, we do not mention anger on ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא heads off a possible objection. It says the verse from Step 1 is still excluded, even though רב נחמן viewed it positively.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think this verse is really good news, since רב נחמן welcomed such anger if it brings redemption. The גמרא answers that the outcome may be good, but the wording itself is anger. On ראש השנה, the day of judgment, we avoid mentioning anger at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The beginning of the year, ראש השנה

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not arguing with the משנה. He agrees the verse is about anger; he only says he would gladly accept that anger for the sake of redemption. The rule looks at the verse's wording, not its final outcome.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: And even though Rav Nachman said:
Any anger like this
let the Holy One, blessed be He, be angry at us
and let Him redeem us,
since it was said in anger
mentioning anger on Rosh HaShanah
we do not mention.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms that the verse in Step 1 stays excluded despite רב נחמן's positive reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wording of anger is excluded on ראש השנה even if the anger leads to redemption.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the principle for the whole sugya: what matters is whether the verse's language speaks of anger or punishment.

steps.title: Examples of forbidden זכרונות and שופרות verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives an example of a punishment verse for זכרונות and one for שופרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: זכרון, for example: 'So He remembered that they were but flesh, etc.' שופר, for example: 'Sound the שופר in גבעה, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list of forbidden examples. It gives one punishment verse each for זכרונות and שופרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'He remembered that they were but flesh' speaks of remembering ישראל's weakness after they sinned, not a hopeful remembrance. 'Sound the shofar in Giva' is an alarm warning of disaster coming to ישראל. Both belong to the right categories, but their content is פורענות.

phrases.english: Remembrance, for example:
"So He remembered that they were but flesh, etc."
Shofar, for example:
"Sound the shofar in Giva, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of examples from Step 1 with the other two categories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זכרונות and שופרות verses that speak of punishment for ישראל are not said.

steps.title: Exception: punishment of the nations may be said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the משנה's rule: verses about punishment of the נכרים may be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if one comes to say Kingship, remembrance, and shofar verses about the punishment of the nations, he may say them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the משנה's rule. It sets up a list of allowed examples, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban covers only punishment aimed at ישראל. Punishment of our enemies is really good news for ישראל, so it is not 'mentioning anger' against us. These verses are still פורענות verses; they are simply an allowed exception.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these verses stop being punishment verses. They are punishment verses, but the punishment falls on the nations, so they are allowed.

phrases.english: But if one comes to say
Kingship, remembrance, and shofar verses
about the punishment of the nations,
he may say them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ban taught in Steps 1 to 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Punishment verses directed at the נכרים may be said in מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the ראש השנה מוסף can include verses about God defeating the nations.

steps.title: Examples of allowed verses about punishing the nations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives allowed examples for all three categories, each describing God punishing the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: מלכות, for example: 'The Lord reigns, let the peoples tremble,' and: 'The Lord is King for ever and ever; the nations have perished out of His land.' זכרון, for example: 'Remember, O Lord, against the children of אדום, etc.' שופר, for example: 'And the Lord God will sound the שופר and will go with whirlwinds of the south,' and it is written: 'The Lord of hosts will defend them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא illustrates the exception from Step 4 with real verses for מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each verse the anger is aimed at the nations: the peoples tremble, the nations perish, and God remembers Edom's crimes. For the שופר verse, the גמרא quotes the next verse, 'The Lord of hosts will defend them.' That shows the shofar blast is protection for ישראל, not a punishment of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Edom, an enemy nation of ישראל
And it is written (bringing a supporting verse)

phrases.english: Kingship, for example:
"The Lord reigns, let the peoples tremble,"
and, for example: "The Lord is King for ever and ever;
the nations have perished out of His land."
Remembrance, for example:
"Remember, O Lord, against the children of Edom, etc."
Shofar, for example:
"And the Lord God will sound the shofar
and will go with whirlwinds of the south,"
and it is written: "The Lord of hosts will defend them."
phrases.notes: Zechariah 9:15, showing the verse protects ישראל

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the examples for the exception stated in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Verses showing God's anger directed at the nations, for ישראל's benefit, are allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Punishment against ישראל is not said on ראש השנה. Punishment against the nations, which protects ישראל, may be said.

steps.title: No verses of an individual's remembrance, even for good
steps.stepSummary: We do not say a זכרונות verse about the remembrance of a יחיד, even when it is for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not mention the remembrance of an individual, even for good, for example: 'Remember me, O Lord, when You show favor to Your people,' and, for example: 'Remember me, my God, for good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a separate rule about זכרונות: verses where one person asks to be remembered are not used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These verses are positive, so the problem is not punishment. The problem is that they speak of a single person ('remember me'), while the ראש השנה זכרונות are about the community as a whole. So 'even for good' tells us this is a new reason for leaving a verse out, not the punishment reason.
steps.whatToRemember: Two kinds of verses are left out of זכרונות: punishment verses against ישראל, and verses about a יחיד's remembrance, even positive ones.

phrases.english: We do not mention the remembrance of an individual,
even for good,
for example: "Remember me, O Lord, when You show favor to Your people,"
and, for example: "Remember me, my God, for good."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the punishment rule to a new rule about individual remembrance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זכרונות verse about an individual is not said, even if it asks for good.

steps.title: Do verses of 'visiting' count as remembrance verses?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יוסי says פקדונות verses count as זכרונות. רבי יהודה says they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Verses about God 'visiting' (פקדונות) are like remembrance verses. For example: 'And ה׳ visited שרה,' and 'I have surely visited you.' This is the view of רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says: they are not like remembrance verses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about which verses may be used for the זכרונות section of מוסף on ראש השנה. רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה argue about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word פקד ('visited' or 'took note of') means almost the same as זכר ('remembered'). רבי יוסי says the meaning is enough, so these verses count. רבי יהודה says only verses that actually speak of remembering count.

keyTerms.meaning: Verses that speak of God 'visiting' or taking note of someone (from the root פקד)
The section of מוסף on ראש השנה made up of verses about God remembering
These are the words of רבי יוסי (marks whose opinion this is)

steps.confusionAlert: פקדונות here does NOT mean 'deposits' (the more common meaning of פקדון in the גמרא). Here it means verses of God 'visiting' or remembering, from פקד.

phrases.english: Verses of 'visiting' are like remembrance verses,
for example: 'And ה׳ visited Sarah,'
and for example: 'I have surely visited you,'
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says: they are not like remembrance verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues listing rules about which verses may be used in זכרונות. It adds a new question: do פקידה verses count?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: פקידה verses count as זכרונות. רבי יהודה: they do not.

steps.title: But the verse about שרה is about one person
steps.stepSummary: Even if רבי יוסי counts פקידה verses, his example about שרה is about a single person. We already learned that we do not say זכרונות verses about a יחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוסי: fine, let us say that 'visiting' verses are like remembrance verses. But 'And ה׳ visited שרה' is a visiting of an individual!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's example. The challenge uses the rule from Step 6: we do not say a remembrance verse about one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא accepts רבי יוסי's main idea that פקידה equals זכירה. It only attacks the example he chose. The verse about שרה seems to break the rule against verses about a יחיד, even though it is for good.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / even if we accept that

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yosei, granted
that 'visiting' verses are like remembrance verses,
'And ה׳ visited Sarah' —
that is a visiting of an individual!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the example in רבי יוסי's statement from Step 7, using the rule from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's use of 'וה׳ פקד את שרה' as a זכרונות verse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We do not say זכרונות verses about a יחיד, even for good (Step 6). The verse about שרה is about one person, so it should not be allowed.

steps.title: שרה counts as many, because the nation came from her
steps.stepSummary: Since a whole nation came from שרה, a verse about her counts as a verse about many people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since many people came from her, she is like many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שרה is not treated as an ordinary individual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When God remembered שרה and she had יצחק, this led to the whole Jewish people. So remembering her is really remembering the many. The rule against verses about a יחיד stays in place, and שרה is a special exception.

keyTerms.meaning: She is considered like many people

steps.whatToRemember: The rule is that זכרונות verses must be about the many. A person who is the source of the whole nation, like שרה, counts as 'many'.

phrases.english: Since many came from her —
she is considered like many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition: the individual is reclassified as 'many'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse about שרה is about one person, so it should be banned like other verses about a יחיד.
steps.terutzMaskana: שרה is the mother of the whole nation, so remembering her counts as remembering the many. The verse is allowed.

steps.title: Counting the kingship verses in 'Lift up your heads, O gates': רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: About the verses 'שאו שערים ראשיכם', רבי יוסי says the first half counts as two מלכיות verses and the second half counts as three.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Lift up your heads, O gates, and be lifted up, everlasting doors, so the King of glory may come in. Who is this King of glory? ה׳ strong and mighty, ה׳ mighty in battle. Lift up your heads, O gates, and lift up, everlasting doors, so the King of glory may come in. Who is this King of glory? ה׳ of hosts, He is the King of glory, Selah.' The first half counts as two, the second half counts as three. This is the view of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a passage from תהלים כ״ד and starts a new dispute: how many מלכיות verses does it contain? This step gives רבי יוסי's count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first half, 'מלך הכבוד' appears twice: 'ויבוא מלך הכבוד' and the question 'מי זה מלך הכבוד'. In the second half it appears three times: in the statement, in the question, and in the answer 'ה׳ צבאות הוא מלך הכבוד'. רבי יוסי counts every mention, even the one inside a question.

keyTerms.meaning: The section of מוסף made up of verses about God's kingship
The first one (here: the first half of the passage)
The second one (here: the second half of the passage)

phrases.english: 'Lift up your heads, O gates,'
and be lifted up, everlasting doors,
so that the King of glory may come in.
Who is this King of glory?

phrases.aramaic: ה׳ עִזּוּז וְגִבּוֹר ה׳ גִּבּוֹר מִלְחָמָה.
phrases.english: ה׳ strong and mighty, ה׳ mighty in battle.
Lift up your heads, O gates,
and lift up, everlasting doors,
so that the King of glory may come in.
Who then is this King of glory?

phrases.aramaic: ה׳ צְבָאוֹת הוּא מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד סֶלָה״.
phrases.english: ה׳ of hosts, He is the King of glory, Selah.'
The first half counts as two,
the second half counts as three,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׂאוּ שְׁעָרִים רָאשֵׁיכֶם וְהִנָּשְׂאוּ פִּתְחֵי עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from זכרונות to a new question about counting מלכיות verses. The disputants are again רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי counts every mention of 'מלך הכבוד', even inside the question. The first half gives two מלכיות verses and the second half gives three.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's lower count: the question does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the first half counts as one מלכיות verse and the second half counts as two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the first half counts as one, the second half counts as two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the dispute. רבי יהודה counts one less in each half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not count the question 'מי זה מלך הכבוד' as a statement of God's kingship. A question is not a declaration of praise. So each half loses one: the first half has one, the second half has two.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument is about the question 'מי זה מלך הכבוד'. רבי יוסי counts it as a kingship mention. רבי יהודה does not. That is why רבי יהודה's numbers are always one lower in each half.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
the first half counts as one,
the second half counts as two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing count to רבי יוסי's view in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה does not count the question 'מי זה מלך הכבוד'. The first half has one מלכיות verse and the second half has two.

steps.title: How many Kingship verses are in 'Sing praises to God'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי counts the פסוקים 'זמרו אלהים... כי מלך כל הארץ אלהים' as two מלכיות verses. רבי יהודה counts them as only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Sing praises to God, sing praises, sing praises to our King, sing praises. For God is the King of all the earth." These count as two, says רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says: only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives another example of the same argument we saw with 'שאו שערים'. Here the question is how many מלכיות verses these פסוקים count as.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי counts 'זמרו למלכנו' as one mention of God as King and 'כי מלך כל הארץ אלהים' as a second. רבי יהודה counts only one. 'למלכנו' calls God only 'our King', so for him it is not a full statement of God's kingship over the world.

keyTerms.meaning: Two / one (how many verses it counts as)

phrases.english: "Sing praises to God, sing praises,
sing praises to our King, sing praises.
For God is the King of all the earth"
These count as two; these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says: only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתַּיִם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example of the counting מחלוקת, parallel to 'שאו שערים' in steps 10 and 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי counts these פסוקים as two מלכיות verses. רבי יהודה counts them as one.

steps.title: Both agree that 'God reigns over the nations' counts once
steps.stepSummary: Both רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה agree that 'מלך אלהים על גוים אלהים ישב על כסא קדשו' counts as only one מלכיות verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both agree about "God reigns over the nations, God sits upon His holy throne": it counts as only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now points out a case where both תנאים agree. This pasuk counts as only one מלכיות verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מלך אלהים על גוים' is a clear statement of kingship. 'ישב על כסא קדשו' (sitting on His throne) hints at kingship but never actually uses the word 'king'. So even רבי יוסי, who counts generously, will not count the second half separately.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the limit of רבי יוסי's counting. He counts only phrases that actually speak of God as King, not images that merely suggest kingship.

phrases.english: And they agree regarding "God reigns over the nations,
God sits upon His holy throne",
that it counts as only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the boundary of the מחלוקת in step 12: a case where even רבי יוסי counts only once.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that 'מלך אלהים על גוים אלהים ישב על כסא קדשו' is one מלכיות verse.

steps.title: A זכרון verse that mentions the שופר blast
steps.stepSummary: A זכרון verse that also says 'תרועה' may be said in זכרונות or in שופרות according to רבי יוסי. According to רבי יהודה, it goes only in זכרונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A remembrance verse that also mentions a תרועה, for example "A solemn rest, a remembrance of תרועה, a holy gathering": one may say it with the זכרונות, and one may also say it with the שופרות. These are the words of רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says: one says it only with the זכרונות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a new question: where do you put a פסוק that fits two categories? Here the פסוק mentions both remembrance and a תרועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the word תרועה is enough to count as a שופר verse, so this פסוק can be used in either section. For רבי יהודה, a שופרות verse must actually say 'שופר'. Since the word תרועה alone is not enough for him, the פסוק belongs only in זכרונות.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה rejects this פסוק. He agrees it is a good זכרונות verse. He only disagrees that it can also be used for שופרות.

phrases.english: A remembrance verse that has a mention of sounding in it
for example: "A solemn rest, a remembrance of sounding, a holy gathering"
one may say it with the remembrances

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמְרָהּ עִם הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: and one may say it with the shofar verses; these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אוֹמְרָהּ אֶלָּא עִם הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: one says it only with the remembrances alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how many times a פסוק counts to which section a mixed-category פסוק belongs in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: a זכרון verse with תרועה may go in זכרונות or שופרות. רבי יהודה: only in זכרונות.

steps.title: A מלכות verse that mentions the שופר blast
steps.stepSummary: A מלכות verse that also says 'תרועה' may be said in מלכיות or in שופרות according to רבי יוסי. According to רבי יהודה, it goes only in מלכיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Kingship verse that has a תרועה with it, for example "ה׳ his God is with him, and the תרועה of a King is among them": one may say it with the מלכיות, and one may also say it with the שופרות. These are the words of רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says: one says it only with the מלכיות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the same argument as the step before, now applied to a מלכיות verse that also mentions a תרועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is identical. רבי יוסי treats 'תרועה' as a valid שופר mention, so the פסוק fits both sections. רבי יהודה needs the actual word 'שופר', so the פסוק stays only in מלכיות.

keyTerms.meaning: The sounding / joyful shout of a King

phrases.english: A Kingship verse that has a mention of sounding with it

phrases.aramaic: — כְּגוֹן: ״ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו עִמּוֹ וּתְרוּעַת מֶלֶךְ בּוֹ״
phrases.english: for example: "The Lord his God is with him, and the sounding of a King is among them"
one may say it with the Kingship verses

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמְרָהּ עִם הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: and one may say it with the shofar verses; these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אוֹמְרָהּ אֶלָּא עִם הַמַּלְכִיּוֹת בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: one says it only with the Kingship verses alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel case to step 14, using מלכיות instead of זכרונות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: a מלכות verse with תרועה may go in מלכיות or שופרות. רבי יהודה: only in מלכיות.

steps.title: A verse that mentions only a sounding and nothing else
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק that mentions only 'תרועה', with no kingship or remembrance, may be said in שופרות according to רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says it is not said at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תרועה verse that has nothing else with it, for example "It shall be a day of תרועה for you": one may say it with the שופרות. These are the words of רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says: one does not say it at all.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last case in the series: a פסוק whose only relevant word is 'תרועה'. Here the two views end up furthest apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, 'תרועה' counts as a שופר mention, so this פסוק is a good שופרות verse. For רבי יהודה, 'תרועה' without the word 'שופר' is not a שופר verse. Since the פסוק fits no other section either, it cannot be used anywhere.
steps.whatToRemember: One idea drives all three תרועה cases. רבי יוסי says the word 'תרועה' counts as a שופר verse. רבי יהודה says a שופרות verse must say 'שופר' outright. So for רבי יוסי a mixed פסוק can go in two places, while for רבי יהודה it goes only in its other category. A פסוק with only 'תרועה' fits nowhere for רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: A sounding verse that has nothing else with it
for example: "It shall be a day of sounding for you"

phrases.aramaic: — אוֹמְרָהּ עִם הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: one may say it with the shofar verses; these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
one does not say it at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תרועה series by removing the other category. This exposes the core disagreement most sharply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: a pure תרועה verse is said in שופרות. רבי יהודה: it is not said at all.

steps.title: The משנה's rule on ending with a verse from the Prophets
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: start with תורה and end with נביא. רבי יוסי says that if one ended with תורה, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: One begins with verses from the תורה and ends with a verse from נביאים. רבי יוסי says: if he ended with the תורה, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה so it can examine it. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each set of ten פסוקים (מלכיות, זכרונות, שופרות) has an order. The תנא קמא says the last פסוק should come from נביא. רבי יוסי says ending with a פסוק from תורה also works.

phrases.english: One begins with the Torah and concludes with the Prophets,
Rabbi Yosei says:
If he concluded with the Torah, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier topic of which פסוקים count to a new line in the משנה about the order of the פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: end with נביא. רבי יוסי: ending with תורה is valid.

steps.title: Reading 'if he concluded' as after-the-fact only
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבי יוסי's wording 'אם השלים' that ending with תורה is only acceptable after the fact, not the ideal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he concluded' means after the fact, yes, it counts. As the preferred way, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a precise inference from רבי יוסי's wording. This inference sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'if he did it' usually describes something already done, not something you should plan to do. So רבי יוסי seems to say ending with תורה is only בדיעבד.

phrases.english: 'If he concluded' implies:
after the fact, yes;
ideally, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of רבי יוסי in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the wording, רבי יוסי allows ending with תורה only בדיעבד.

steps.title: A ברייתא says רבי יוסי praises ending with the תורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי saying that one who ends with תורה is praiseworthy. That means it is the ideal way, which contradicts the inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי says, one who concludes with the תורה is praiseworthy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference by quoting a ברייתא where רבי יוסי openly praises ending with תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You do not call something 'משובח' if it is only acceptable after the fact. So the ברייתא shows that for רבי יוסי, ending with תורה is the best way לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
One who concludes with the Torah is praiseworthy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference made in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that רבי יוסי permits ending with תורה only בדיעבד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls ending with תורה 'משובח', which means it is the ideal practice.

steps.title: Change the wording to 'he concludes'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing רבי יוסי's words in the משנה from 'אם השלים' to 'משלים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'He concludes' with the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by changing the wording of רבי יוסי's statement. Now it says plainly that one should end with תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'משלים' states the ideal way to do it. 'אם השלים' only describes something already done. With the new reading, the משנה matches the ברייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer is refined, not dropped. The next step objects that the משנה really does say 'אם השלים'. The final reading in step 22 keeps 'משלים בתורה' for רבי יוסי and moves the words 'אם השלים' to ending with נביא.

phrases.english: Say: 'He concludes.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Emending the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי allows ending with תורה only after the fact.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי says ending with תורה is the ideal way.

steps.title: But the משנה does say 'if he concluded'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the משנה clearly says 'אם השלים', which means only after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it does teach 'if he concluded', which means after the fact, yes; ideally, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the change in wording. The actual text of the משנה says 'אם השלים', so we cannot simply ignore it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing a word does not explain why the משנה is worded this way. Any answer has to account for the words 'אם השלים' as they stand.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'if he concluded':
after the fact, yes; ideally, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the change in wording proposed in step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The actual words of the משנה are 'אם השלים', and they still imply בדיעבד only.

steps.title: Rereading the משנה: רבי יוסי reverses the roles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה differently. For רבי יוסי, the ideal is to end with תורה. 'אם השלים' refers to ending with נביא, which works after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: One begins with the תורה and concludes with נביאים. רבי יוסי says: one concludes with the תורה, and if he concluded with נביאים, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the משנה. Now the after-the-fact words 'אם השלים' describe ending with נביא, not ending with תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, רבי יוסי holds that ending with תורה is the ideal. Ending with נביא, the way the תנא קמא does it, only works בדיעבד. This fits both the words 'אם השלים' and the ברייתא's praise.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it is saying

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
One begins with the Torah and concludes with the Prophets.
Rabbi Yosei says: one concludes with the Torah,
and if he concluded with the Prophets, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 with a new reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the משנה as a shortened text (הכי קאמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אם השלים' refers to ending with תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אם השלים' refers to ending with נביא. For רבי יוסי, ending with תורה is the ideal.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי: ideally end with a פסוק from תורה. Ending with נביא works after the fact.

steps.title: Support: the ווֹתִיקִין ended with the תורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports this: רבי אלעזר בן רבי יוסי reports that the ווֹתִיקִין used to end with תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי said, the ווֹתִיקִין (pious ones) used to conclude it with the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the new reading. Careful, pious people used to end with תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ווֹתִיקִין, who did every מצוה in the best way, ended with תורה, then ending with תורה is the ideal. This matches רבי יוסי's view, and the report comes from רבי יוסי's own son.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)
pious people, careful in doing מצוות

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei said:
The pious ones used to conclude it with the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading given in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That for רבי יוסי, ending with תורה is the ideal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the ווֹתִיקִין ended with תורה (reported by רבי אלעזר בן רבי יוסי).

steps.title: Not enough מלכיות verses in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: זכרונות and שופרות have many פסוקים in the תורה, but מלכיות has only three. רבי יוסי needs four from the תורה, so his method does not seem to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for זכרונות and שופרות there are many verses. But for מלכיות there are only three: 'ה׳ his God is with him, and the sounding of a king is among them'; 'And He was king in ישורון'; 'ה׳ will reign forever and ever'. And we need ten, and there are not enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a practical problem with רבי יוסי's view. There do not seem to be enough מלכיות פסוקים in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The set of ten opens with three פסוקים from תורה. For רבי יוסי it also ends with a פסוק from תורה, so it needs four תורה פסוקים in total. The תורה seems to have only three מלכיות פסוקים, so his ideal order cannot be completed for מלכיות.
steps.confusionAlert: 'We need ten' does not mean ten from the תורה. The ten includes נביאים and כתובים. The problem is that רבי יוסי's order needs four of the ten to come from the תורה, and only three exist.

phrases.english: Granted, for Remembrances and Shofarot there are many,
but for Kingship there are only three:
'ה׳ his God is with him, and the sounding of a king is among them,'
'And He was king in Yeshurun,'
'ה׳ will reign forever and ever,'
and we need ten, and there are not enough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of steps 22-23 to raise a practical difficulty for רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that one should ideally end each section with a פסוק from תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מלכיות would need four תורה פסוקים (three at the start plus one at the end), but only three are known.

steps.title: רב הונא: for רבי יוסי, שמע counts as Kingship
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes a תוספתא: רבי יוסי counts 'שמע ישראל' as a מלכות פסוק, which gives a fourth one. רבי יהודה disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Come and hear: 'Hear, O Israel, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One' is a Kingship verse. These are the words of רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says: it is not a Kingship verse.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא begins to answer the problem by quoting a teaching. According to רבי יוסי, 'שמע ישראל' is a מלכות פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, 'שמע ישראל' declares ה׳'s kingship, so it counts as a fourth מלכיות פסוק from the תורה. This solves the problem, which was raised only against רבי יוסי's view. רבי יהודה does not count it as a מלכות פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: the first פסוק of קריאת שמע

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי יוסי's view hangs together: his wider definition of a מלכות פסוק is what lets him end מלכיות with a פסוק from תורה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: Come and hear:
'Hear, O Israel, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One':
it is a Kingship verse. These are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says: it is not a Kingship verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing a source that adds another qualifying פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תורה has only three מלכיות פסוקים.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי, 'שמע ישראל' is a fourth מלכות פסוק, so his order works.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי counts 'שמע ישראל' as מלכות, which gives him four תורה פסוקים for מלכיות. רבי יהודה does not count it.

steps.title: Two more verses that רבי יוסי counts as Kingship
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא continues. It adds two more פסוקים from ספר דברים that רבי יוסי counts as מלכות and רבי יהודה rejects.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Know this day and take it to your heart that ה׳ is God, there is no other' counts as a Kingship verse, says רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says it does not. 'You were shown, so that you would know that ה׳ is God, there is none besides Him' counts as a Kingship verse, says רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same תוספתא from the last step. It lists two more verses that רבי יוסי treats as מלכות verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24 the problem was that the תורה seemed to have only three מלכות verses, but רבי יוסי needs four. Step 25 added 'שמע ישראל' as a fourth. These two extra verses make the count even more comfortable. So רבי יוסי can open with three verses from the תורה and close with one more, as his view requires.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse about ה׳'s Kingship, used in the מלכיות section of מוסף
It is not a Kingship verse

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, verses that declare ה׳ is the only God count as מלכות. This gives him enough תורה verses to end with a תורה verse. רבי יהודה only counts verses that speak of ה׳ as King.

phrases.english: "Know this day and take it to your heart

phrases.aramaic: כִּי ה׳ הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים אֵין עוֹד״
phrases.english: that the LORD is God, there is no other"
is a Kingship verse; these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says: it is not a Kingship verse.
"You were shown, so that you would know

phrases.aramaic: כִּי ה׳ הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים אֵין עוֹד מִלְבַדּוֹ״
phrases.english: that the LORD is God, there is none besides Him"
is a Kingship verse; these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says: it is not a Kingship verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַלְכוּת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינָהּ מַלְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same תוספתא quoted in step 25 and finishes answering the problem from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds more verses that count under רבי יוסי's wider definition of מלכות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תורה has only three מלכות verses, so רבי יוסי cannot end with a תורה verse.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי, verses about ה׳ being the only God also count, so he has plenty of תורה verses.

steps.title: New משנה: the second leader blows שופר, the first leader says הלל
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that on ראש השנה the שופר is blown by the second חזן (מוסף). On days with הלל, the first חזן (שחרית) leads הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the יום טוב of ראש השנה, among those who lead the prayers, the second one (the מוסף leader) has the שופר blown. On days when הלל is said, the first one (the שחרית leader) leads הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us which of the two prayer leaders handles the שופר and which handles הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each day has two prayer leaders: one for שחרית and one for מוסף. The שופר is attached to the second one, during מוסף. הלל is attached to the first one, during שחרית. This difference sets up the question in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who 'passes before the ark', meaning the חזן leading the prayers
The second leader, the one who leads מוסף
The first leader, the one who leads שחרית
Has the שופר blown (he oversees the blowing)
The praise chapters of תהלים said on יום טוב and ראש חודש

steps.confusionAlert: 'Second' and 'first' do not mean the second or first day of the holiday. They mean the second and first prayer leader of the same day: מוסף and שחרית.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who passes before the ark (leads prayers)
on the festival of Rosh HaShana,
the second one has the shofar blown.
And at a time when Hallel is said,
the first one leads the Hallel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שופר is blown in מוסף, by the second חזן. הלל is said in שחרית, by the first חזן.

steps.title: Why does the second leader blow the shofar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the שופר goes with the second חזן. It suggests a reason: 'ברוב עם הדרת מלך', since more people are present later in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about the second leader that he blows the שופר? Is it because 'the King's glory is in a large crowd'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's שופר rule and suggests one possible answer. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested reason is that by מוסף more people have arrived in shul. Doing the מצוה in front of a bigger crowd brings more honor to ה׳. That would explain why the שופר waits until מוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why is this case treated differently?
'The King's glory is in a large crowd' (משלי יד:כח). It is better to do מצוות with many people present.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is different that the second one blows the shofar?
Is it because "In a large crowd is the King's glory"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the שופר rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the שופר is blown by the מוסף leader and not the שחרית leader.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suggested: because of ברוב עם הדרת מלך, since more people are there by מוסף.

steps.title: Then הלל should also be by the second leader
steps.stepSummary: If a bigger crowd is the reason, הלל should also wait for the second חזן. Yet the משנה gives הלל to the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then הלל too: let us say it with the second leader, because 'the King's glory is in a large crowd'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason it just suggested. That reason would also move הלל to מוסף, which goes against the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A good reason should explain the whole משנה. The 'large crowd' reason applies to הלל just as much as to שופר. So it cannot explain why the משנה treats them differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say (do it this way)

phrases.english: If so, Hallel too
let us say it with the second leader
because "In a large crowd is the King's glory"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason suggested in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason ברוב עם הדרת מלך given for the שופר rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reason would require הלל to be said with the second leader too, but the משנה says the first leader says it.

steps.title: Trying the other direction: הלל is early because of eagerness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the approach. Maybe the key is הלל: it is said early because 'זריזין מקדימין למצוות', eager people do מצוות as early as they can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is special about הלל that it is said with the first leader? It is because the eager do מצוות early.
steps.whatsHappening: Using 'אלא' (rather), the גמרא drops the first idea and tries a new reason, this time starting from the הלל rule. This sets up another challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the basic rule is that מצוות should be done as early as possible. That explains why הלל is said in שחרית.

keyTerms.meaning: Eager people do מצוות early, as soon as they can

phrases.english: Rather: what is different about Hallel that it is with the first leader?
It is because the eager do מצוות early,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first reason failed in step 29, tries the opposite reason, starting from הלל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why הלל is said with the first leader.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because of זריזין מקדימין למצוות, the rule of doing מצוות early.

steps.title: Then שופר should also be by the first leader
steps.stepSummary: If doing מצוות early is the reason, the שופר should also be blown by the first חזן. The next step explains why they differ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the שופר too: let us blow it with the first leader, because the eager do מצוות early!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second reason too. It would move the שופר to שחרית, which goes against the משנה. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reason explains one half of the משנה and clashes with the other half. 'Large crowd' fits שופר but not הלל, and 'do it early' fits הלל but not שופר. The גמרא now needs a special reason why the שופר in particular was moved later.
steps.whatToRemember: Two general rules pull in opposite directions: ברוב עם הדרת מלך (wait for a crowd) and זריזין מקדימין למצוות (do it early). The משנה follows one rule for הלל and the other for שופר. The גמרא must explain why.

phrases.english: Then the shofar blowing too, let us do it with the first leader,
because the eager do מצוות early!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason suggested in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason זריזין מקדימין למצוות given for the הלל rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reason would require the שופר to be blown with the first leader, but the משנה says the second leader blows it.

steps.title: The שופר was moved later because of persecution
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the משנה's rule of blowing שופר at מוסף was set during a time of persecution.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They taught this rule during a time of persecution.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finally answers the question raised in Steps 28–31: why the שופר goes with the second חזן, but הלל goes with the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither 'a bigger crowd' nor 'doing מצוות early' explained the difference. רבי יוחנן gives a historical reason instead. The non-Jewish government once banned blowing שופר and watched the Jews in the early morning, so the blowing was pushed off to מוסף after the guards had left. There was no such ban on הלל, so הלל stayed early, following the rule of זריזין מקדימין.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of persecution, when the government outlawed Jewish practice
They taught (referring to the rule in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the שופר is blown at מוסף because מוסף is a better time. The reason is historical: blowing early was dangerous. The custom stayed in place even after the danger passed.
steps.whatToRemember: שופר at מוסף came from a time of persecution. הלל stays at שחרית because people eager for מצוות do them early.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the practice still followed today of blowing the main תקיעות around מוסף.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
They taught this in a time of persecution.
phrases.notes: The guards left by מוסף time, so blowing was delayed until then.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בִּשְׁעַת הַשְּׁמָד שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty left standing in Step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between שופר and הלל must come from a general principle, like crowd size or eagerness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שופר was moved later only because of a persecution decree. Otherwise, the principle of eagerness applies, which is why הלל is early.

steps.title: Inferring that there is no הלל on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's words 'at the time of הלל', the גמרא infers that ראש השנה itself has no הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה says 'at the time of הלל', we can infer that on ראש השנה there is no הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads closely into the wording of the משנה and pulls out a new fact. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה spoke about ראש השנה and then switched to 'days when הלל is said'. That switch shows those must be other days, like the other festivals. So ראש השנה must not have הלל at all.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it says

phrases.english: From the fact that it says "at the time of Hallel",
it follows that on Rosh Hashanah there is no Hallel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the timing question to a new point drawn from the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no הלל on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Why is there no הלל on ראש השנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that ראש השנה has no הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ראש השנה, a יום טוב, does not get הלל. This sets up רבי אבהו's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other holidays have הלל, so it is surprising that ראש השנה does not. The גמרא wants the reason behind this.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the inference in Step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why הלל is not said on ראש השנה.

steps.title: No songs of joy while the books of life and death are open
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו relates that the angels asked הקדוש ברוך הוא why ישראל do not sing on ראש השנה and יום כיפור. He answered that singing does not fit while He sits in judgment with the books of life and death open.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The מלאכי השרת said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: 'רבונו של עולם! Why don't ישראל sing before You on ראש השנה and יום כיפור?' He said to them: 'Is it possible that the King sits on the throne of judgment, with the books of life and the books of death open before Him, and ישראל should be singing?!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question with a story. These are days of judgment, and joyful songs of praise like הלל do not fit that serious mood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל is a joyous song of praise. On ראש השנה and יום כיפור, every person's life is being decided. The fitting mood is serious and fearful, not celebratory, so הלל is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Song of praise (here referring to הלל)
Books of life and books of death

steps.whatToRemember: No הלל on ראש השנה or יום כיפור, because they are days of judgment, not days for joyful singing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the ימים נוראים have no הלל, even though other holidays do.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
The ministering angels said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world!
For what reason do the Jewish people not
say song before You
on Rosh Hashanah and on Yom Kippur?
He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר מֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא דִין,
phrases.english: Is it possible that the King sits on the throne of judgment,
and the books of life and the books of death
are open before Him —
and the Jewish people should be saying song?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Days of judgment are not fitting for joyful songs of praise, so הלל is not said.

steps.title: New משנה: the שופר does not override שבת-type prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that to get or prepare a שופר on ראש השנה, one may not break any prohibition, Torah-level or rabbinic. Examples include walking past the תחום, clearing a rubble pile, climbing a tree, riding an animal, swimming, or cutting the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: For the שופר of ראש השנה, one may not go past the תחום, and one may not clear away a pile of rubble to get it. One may not climb a tree, ride on an animal, or swim across water to get it. And one may not cut it into shape, whether the act is forbidden by a rabbinic decree (שבות) or by a לא תעשה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists actions that are forbidden on יום טוב, and teaches that the מצוה of שופר does not permit any of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though שופר is a Torah מצוה, it does not push aside the rules of the day. This holds for Torah-level prohibitions and also for rabbinic ones (שבות), like climbing a tree or riding an animal. If getting a שופר requires breaking one of these, one simply does without.

keyTerms.meaning: The boundary one may walk to on שבת or יום טוב
Clearing away a pile of rubble
A rabbinic prohibition for שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that a big Torah מצוה like שופר automatically overrides only the 'small' rabbinic rules. The משנה says it overrides neither the rabbinic rules nor the Torah ones.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The shofar of Rosh Hashanah —
one may not go past the Shabbos boundary for it,
and one may not clear away a pile of rubble for it.
One may not climb a tree,
and one may not ride on an animal,
and one may not swim on the water,
and one may not cut it —
whether with something forbidden by a rabbinic decree,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין בְּדָבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: or with something forbidden by a Torah prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שׁוֹפָר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אֵין מַעֲבִירִין עָלָיו אֶת הַתְּחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה of שופר does not override any שבת or יום טוב prohibition, Torah-level or rabbinic.

steps.title: Putting water or wine into the שופר is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows placing water or wine into the שופר on ראש השנה to improve its sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if one wants to put water or wine into it, he may put it in.
steps.whatsHappening: After the list of forbidden actions, the משנה gives one thing that is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting liquid into a שופר makes its sound clearer. This is not a forbidden מלאכה, so it is allowed on יום טוב.

phrases.english: But if he wants
to put water or wine into it —
he may put it in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אִם רָצָה לִיתֵּן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם אוֹ יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a permitted action in contrast to the forbidden list in Step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may put water or wine into a שופר on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Children may practice blowing שופר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that children are not stopped from blowing שופר on ראש השנה, and adults may help them until they learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not stop children from blowing the שופר. Rather, we work with them until they learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to children. Even though they are not yet obligated, they may blow the שופר on יום טוב, and adults may train them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that blowing on יום טוב with no obligation is just making noise and should be stopped. The משנה allows it for the sake of חינוך. Adults may even actively teach the children.

phrases.english: We do not stop the children from blowing,
rather, we work with them
until they learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a new rule about children.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children may blow שופר on ראש השנה, and adults may train them.

steps.title: Blowing without intent does not count
steps.stepSummary: A person who blows שופר without intending the מצוה does not fulfill it, and neither does someone who listens to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who blows without intent has not fulfilled the מצוה, and one who hears from someone blowing without intent has not fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by teaching that blowing שופר only counts if it is done with intent for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מתעסק is someone who blows without meaning to do the מצוה, for example just practicing or playing around. His blowing does not count for himself. Since it is not a real מצוה blowing, listeners cannot fulfill their obligation through him either.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone acting without intent for the מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: שופר does not override יום טוב prohibitions. Water or wine may be put in. Children may practice. Blowing without intent for the מצוה does not count, for the blower or for the listeners.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is an important source for the larger discussion of whether מצוות require intent (מצוות צריכות כוונה).

phrases.english: And one who acts without intent — has not fulfilled his obligation,
and one who hears from one acting without intent — has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the rule about children practicing by noting that practice blowing without intent does not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blowing without intent for the מצוה does not fulfill the obligation, and listening to such blowing does not either.

steps.title: Why can't the שופר מצוה override יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why one may not break a prohibition to get or prepare a שופר, since a positive מצוה usually overrides a negative one.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking for the reason behind its rule. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that עשה דוחה לא תעשה: a positive command can push aside a negative command. So we might expect blowing שופר to permit work on יום טוב. The גמרא wants to know why the משנה forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that comes after the משנה
The rule that a positive command overrides a negative command (assumed in the background here)

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא on the new משנה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why can't the positive מצוה of שופר override the prohibitions?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule in step 36 that no prohibition may be broken for a שופר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the positive מצוה of שופר does not override the prohibitions of יום טוב, given the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה.

steps.title: יום טוב has both a positive and a negative command
steps.stepSummary: שופר is only a positive command, while יום טוב is guarded by both a positive and a negative command. A positive command cannot override both together.
steps.simpleTranslation: שופר is a positive command, and יום טוב is both a positive command and a negative command. A positive command does not push aside a negative command together with a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The positive מצוה of שופר is not strong enough to override יום טוב, because יום טוב is protected by two commands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing forbidden work on יום טוב breaks the negative command not to work and also the positive command to rest (שבתון). The rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה only works against a plain negative command. When a positive command stands next to the negative one, the single עשה of שופר loses.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive command (something you must do)
A negative command (something you must not do)
A Festival day, on which certain work is forbidden

keyTerms.term: אֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה
keyTerms.meaning: A positive command does not override a negative command that is joined by a positive command

steps.whatToRemember: One עשה can override a plain לא תעשה, but it cannot override a לא תעשה that comes together with an עשה. That is why work is forbidden on יום טוב even for a שופר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle appears in many places in ש״ס. It explains why positive מצוות generally cannot push aside the laws of שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: Shofar is a positive command,
and a Festival is a positive command and a negative command —
phrases.notes: The positive command is to rest; the negative command is not to do work.

phrases.english: and a positive command does not override
a negative command together with a positive command.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹפָר עֲשֵׂה הוּא, וְיוֹם טוֹב עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 40.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יום טוב is protected by both an עשה and a לא תעשה, and a single עשה like שופר cannot override both together.

steps.title: Why list Torah prohibitions after rabbinic ones?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks: once it has already said that even rabbinic prohibitions may not be broken for a שופר, why must it also say this about Torah-level prohibitions?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught: 'One may not climb a tree, and one may not ride on an animal,' and so on. Now that you said rabbinic prohibitions are not allowed, is it necessary to say that Torah prohibitions are not allowed?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and challenges how it is written. If even a light rabbinic rule may not be broken, then a serious Torah rule is obviously forbidden too. So why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Climbing a tree and riding an animal are only rabbinic prohibitions (שבות), made as safeguards. The משנה then also forbids Torah-level work, such as cutting the שופר. The challenge is that the Torah-level case seems obvious once the lighter rabbinic case is already forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule made by the Rabbis
A rule from the Torah itself
Now; 'now that…', used to start this kind of 'obvious' challenge
A rabbinic prohibition on שבת or יום טוב, made as a safeguard

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is questioning the law itself. Everyone agrees that Torah prohibitions are forbidden. The question is only about why the משנה bothered to write something so obvious.

phrases.english: One may not climb a tree

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא רוֹכְבִין עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: and one may not ride on an animal, etc.
Now that you said rabbinic [prohibitions] are not [permitted],
is it necessary [to say this about] Torah [prohibitions]?!
phrases.notes: For example, cutting the שופר, which the משנה lists afterward.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּרַבָּנַן אָמְרַתְּ לָא, דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason behind the rule to a question about how the משנה is worded.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה in step 36, which lists Torah-level prohibitions after rabbinic ones.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר logic: if even the lighter rabbinic prohibitions are forbidden, the stricter Torah prohibitions are obviously forbidden, so mentioning them seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The משנה uses a 'this, and needless to say that' style
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses the style 'this, and it is unnecessary to say that.' It states the more surprising case and then adds the obvious one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches 'this, and it is unnecessary to say that.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is written in a familiar teaching style. It gives the surprising rule first and then adds the obvious one, as if to say 'and of course this too.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is in the rabbinic cases: even a light rabbinic rule may not be broken for a שופר. The Torah-level case adds nothing new. It is mentioned only to round out the list, in the style 'needless to say.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'This, and needless to say that': a teaching style that states one case and then adds a more obvious one

steps.whatToRemember: When a משנה lists a case that seems obvious, the גמרא may explain that it is using the style 'זו ואין צריך לומר זו.' The obvious case is added only for completeness.

phrases.english: "This, and it is unnecessary to say that"
is what it teaches.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 42.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic explanation of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing Torah prohibitions after rabbinic ones is pointless, since they are obviously included.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה deliberately uses the 'זו ואין צריך לומר זו' style. The Torah-level case is added as the obvious follow-up, and the real new teaching is in the rabbinic cases.
